item.title: West has 'repeatedly failed Assyrian Christians'
item.description: A religious freedom activist warns that the Assyrian Christian community in the Middle East "does not have a chance of survival”.

item.title: 2,000-year-old 'Pilgrim's Path' opens in Jerusalem
item.description: An ancient road that may have been built in the days of Jesus and led up to the Jerusalem Temple Mount has been opened to the public for the first time.

item.title: Christian group welcomes British sanctions on Iranians
item.description: Britain stopped shot of designating the Revolutionary Guard a terrorist organisation.

item.title: Pastor, daughter and son-in-law slain in Plateau state, Nigeria
item.description: Fulani herdsmen last month killed a pastor, his daughter and her husband, leaving the couple’s 3-month-old baby with a machete wound, in Plateau state, Nigeria.

item.title: Prince and Princess of Wales visit Lambeth Palace to meet new Archbishop of Canterbury
item.description: The Prince and Princess of Wales have paid an official visit to Lambeth Palace.

item.title: New research sheds light on why women are more religious than men
item.description: Gender gaps were found to narrow in line with degrees of modernisation, secularisation, and gender equality. But, the paper finds, the "gap does not vanish entirely – even in highly secular countries women remain more religious than men".

item.title: St William shrine fragments return to York Minster after 500 years underground
item.description: Fragments of a long-lost medieval shrine honouring St William of York have returned to York Minster for the first time in nearly 500 years, marking a major moment in the cathedral’s history and a highlight of its programme for 2026.

item.title: Church of England directs £600,000 towards clergy mental health and financial support
item.description: The funding package includes new grants for two national charities working with clergy facing psychological strain and financial pressure.

item.title: Turkey taken to task over Christians banned from the country
item.description: Foreign pastors are often labelled "national security" threats.

item.title: Cuban bishops warn oil sanctions could deepen hardship and unrest
item.description: The message, read in Catholic parishes nationwide, warned that further pressure on fuel access would fall most heavily on vulnerable families already struggling to survive.
